title: Pumpkin pie chia pudding
equipment: Medium bowl or 1-quart jar with lid

items: 1 cup milk (dairy or unsweetened plant milk)
⅓ cup canned pumpkin purée (not pumpkin pie filling)
1 Tbsp maple syrup, plus more to taste

steps: Whisk the milk, pumpkin, maple syrup, spice, vanilla and salt in the bowl until smooth, with no orange streaks.
Whisk in the chia seeds. Let it sit 10 min, then whisk again to break up any clumps.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hr, or overnight, until thick and spoonable.
Toast the pepitas in the dry skillet over medium heat 3–4 min, shaking the pan, until they puff and start to pop. Let them cool.
Stir the pudding, taste and add more maple syrup if you like. Divide between 2 jars and top each with 2 Tbsp yogurt and 1 Tbsp pepitas.
tips: Too thick in the morning? Stir in 1–2 Tbsp milk. Too thin? Stir in 1 tsp chia and wait 15 min.
No pumpkin pie spice: use ¼ tsp cinnamon, ⅛ tsp ground ginger and a pinch each of nutmeg and cloves.
Freeze the rest of the can of pumpkin in ⅓-cup portions for next time.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, covered. Add the yogurt and pepitas just before eating so the pepitas stay crunchy. Don't freeze.
